thread:
jessica: @lee multiple customers reporting 502/504 from hosted inference since ~11:09 UTC. Gateway errors + timeouts, looks like spikes in latency. Any correlation with KV/cache?

cachebot: [ALERT] mem-proxy.svc.cluster: auth_error_rate=7/min, conn_queue_length>1000 at 11:07 UTC

lee: I'm on it, digging into traces now. Do we have mem-proxy and gateway logs aligned?

matt: quick look — mem-proxy started throwing SASL auth failures around 11:06:50, then connection queue length climbed quickly. Gateway has a bunch of upstream 502s referencing memcached timeouts.

jessica: can you paste the relevant log lines?

matt: sure — tail from mem-proxy and gateway around the incident window:

```
[11:06:50] mem-proxy[pid=122] ERROR auth: SASL PLAIN failed for client=10.0.5.22 token=expired_user_token
[11:06:50] mem-proxy[pid=122] WARN connq: queue_length=432 wait_ms=120
[11:07:03] mem-proxy[pid=122] WARN connq: queue_length=980 wait_ms=620
[11:07:14] mem-proxy[pid=122] ERROR auth: SASL PLAIN failed for client=10.0.5.23 token=expired_user_token
[11:07:14] mem-proxy[pid=122] WARN connq: queue_length=1320 wait_ms=860
[11:07:18] gateway[pid=78] ERROR upstream 502 memcache_timeout reason=conn_queue_deadline
[11:07:20] gateway[pid=78] ERROR upstream 504 memcache_connect_timeout backend=mem-proxy
```

amy: metrics show prefix-cache fanout (prefetch) jumped from ~1.2k/s to ~8.9k/s at 11:06:45 — that multiplied all connections and amplified the auth failure storm.

lee: so chain is: auth token rotation or bad creds -> mem-proxy rejects -> client retries and opens new connections -> conn queue on proxies -> upstream timeouts -> gateway 502/504.

jessica: customers are seeing errors and some billing alerts triggered. What's a quick mitigation we can do to reduce customer impact?

matt: two quick knobs: 1) force route to bypass prefix cache (will increase origin load but avoids mem-proxy), 2) temporarily increase mem-proxy conn pool and reduce prefetch fanout. I can flip bypass for a canary zone first.

jessica: go ahead for us-west-2a canary. Provide commands so I can escalate if needed.

matt: commands I ran:

```
# dry-run to confirm
rbctl routes update --route hosted-api --set prefix_cache.enabled=false --zone us-west-2a --dry-run
# apply
rbctl routes update --route hosted-api --set prefix_cache.enabled=false --zone us-west-2a
# reduce prefetch fanout globally (temp)
rbctl config set prefetch.fanout_limit 2000
# bump mem-proxy pool size on the node pool (temporary)
rbctl pool update mem-proxy --conn_pool=100
```

amy: after flipping canary we saw a 70% drop in 502s for that zone within 45s. Good sign.

lee: long-term fixes: ensure auth hot-reload for mem-proxy so token rotations don't cause SASL failures; add circuit-break for auth failures that short-circuits to bypass cache after N auth errors; add alerting on conn_queue > 500 and fanout spike > 2000/s. Also add a fallback route that prefers origin for first 60s post-rotation.

matt: root cause note: token rotation job rolled out a stale client image in one region which sent old token format. That triggered SASL rejects across the mem-proxy fleet behind a shared auth endpoint, causing the cascading backoff.

jessica: i've informed CSMs and put a high-priority incident label. Putting an action item list in the incident doc:
- rollback token rotation in affected region (done)
- patch mem-proxy for graceful auth reload (owner: matt)
- implement circuit-break on auth failures (owner: lee)
- add prefetch fanout caps per route (owner: amy)
- postmortem + customer communication draft (owner: jessica)

matt: note for runbook update: when cache auth errors spike, immediate mitigations = bypass prefix cache for affected zone -> reduce prefetch fanout -> bump conn pools if safe -> rollback token or rotate creds -> monitor 502/latency.

amy: monitoring: I've created a temp dashboard with conn_queue, auth_error_rate, prefix_fanout, gateway_502_rate. I'll keep watch for 30m.

lee: I'm keeping the oncall channel open. If anyone sees recurrent SASL lines after rollback ping me.

jessica: thanks all — happy path: customers recovering in canary, rollout rollback in affected region completed. Will follow up with postmortem and send customer notes by EOD. :thumbsup:
